key_insight: The paper introduces a video world model that conditions diffusion-transformer generation on tracked 3D head pose and joint-level hand poses, enabling fine-grained, embodied control of generated video for XR and interactive scenarios.
problem_solved: Current generative video models accept only coarse control signals (e.g., text or keyboard), preventing tight coupling with users' tracked motion; this work closes the gap by enabling camera + hand-conditioned video generation for embodied interaction.
method: Extend diffusion-transformer video models to accept dense 3D head-pose and joint-level hand-pose conditioning signals.

Systematically evaluate alternative conditioning strategies for diffusion transformers and introduce an effective mechanism for integrating 3D head and hand control (pose-token / cross-attention style conditioning).
Combine pose-conditioned generation with camera/head tracking to produce interactive video sequences responsive to user motion and hand gestures.
impact: By enabling fine-grained, motion-driven video synthesis, this approach makes generative world models usable for XR, telepresence, and embodied AI research—giving practitioners a path to tightly couple user motion with realistic scene generation and interaction.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: tracked head + hand poses → conditioning module → diffusion-transformer → generated video frames
Side-by-side comparison: uncontrolled (text-only) vs. head+hand-conditioned video outputs highlighting gesture fidelity
Timeline/grid visual showing camera/head motion + hand pose inputs mapped to corresponding generated frames
Iconography: head, hand skeleton, camera, and a diffusion model block to communicate inputs and model components
paper_title: Generated Reality: Human-centric World Simulation using Interactive Video Generation with Hand and Camera Control
paper_authors: Linxi Xie, Lisong C. Sun, Ashley Neall, Tong Wu, Shengqu Cai
